definition: A primary female sex hormone responsible for regulating the menstrual cycle, thickening the uterine lining, and developing secondary sexual characteristics.
A hormone produced by the corpus luteum after ovulation. It prepares the uterus for pregnancy and has a naturally calming, sedative effect on the brain.
A hormone secreted by the pituitary gland that stimulates the growth of ovarian follicles before the release of an egg.
A hormone that triggers ovulation and the development of the corpus luteum. An 'LH surge' indicates that ovulation is about to occur.
A temporary endocrine structure in the ovaries that develops from an ovarian follicle after an egg is released. It secretes progesterone.
The inner mucosal lining of the uterus, which thickens during the menstrual cycle in preparation for embryo implantation and is shed during menstruation.
A German word meaning 'middle pain,' referring to the one-sided lower abdominal pain associated with ovulation.
Lipid compounds that have hormone-like effects. During menstruation, they cause the uterus to contract to shed the lining, often resulting in cramps.
The release of a mature egg from an ovary, typically occurring around the middle of the menstrual cycle.
Fluid produced by the cervix that changes in consistency throughout the cycle. Around ovulation, it becomes clear and stretchy (like raw egg whites) to help sperm travel.
